subject: Cloud Computing
title: Forgetting to Set Billing Alerts
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Forgetting to Set Billing Alerts.

hook.text: A student spins up GPU instances for a homework project. Two weeks later: a $12,000 bill from AWS. No alerts were set.

buildup.text: Cloud billing is open-ended by default. Without spending limits or alerts, costs run unchecked until someone checks.

discovery.text: Every major cloud provider offers budget alerts. They take five minutes to set up but can prevent financial disaster.

twist.text: Some providers have forgiven massive accidental bills. But there's no guarantee — and the policy varies case by case.

climax.text: Billing alerts are the first thing to configure on any new cloud account. Before any resource, before any code.

punchline.text: Five minutes to set up alerts. Five figures if you don't.

quiz.question: What is the first thing you should configure on a new cloud account?
options: Billing alerts and budget limits to prevent unexpected charges
The most powerful GPU instances for maximum performance
Public access to all storage buckets for easy sharing

details.summary: Organizations have received cloud bills of tens of thousands of dollars after forgetting to set billing alerts. Runaway instances, crypto-mining on compromised accounts, and accidentally provisioned expensive resources generate costs silently until the monthly bill arrives.
details.whyItMatters: Cloud spend without alerts or budgets can spiral out of control. Setting billing alerts is a simple action that prevents financially devastating surprises.
takeaways: Unexpected cloud bills of five to six figures are not uncommon
Compromised accounts used for crypto mining drive huge costs
Billing alerts should be the first thing configured

faq.question: What is the largest accidental cloud bill reported?
faq.answer: Public reports include bills exceeding $72,000 from runaway GPU instances and six-figure bills from compromised accounts used for cryptocurrency mining. The actual largest bills are likely unreported, but major cloud providers sometimes provide one-time credits for honest mistakes.

faq.question: What billing controls should be set up immediately?
faq.answer: Configure budget alerts at 50 percent, 80 percent, and 100 percent of expected spend. Enable anomaly detection. Set hard spending limits where available. Review the cost dashboard weekly. For new accounts, limit the instance types and regions that can be used.
